answer: Each epoch, graders are drawn by verifiable randomness from a large staked pool, and the panel rotates before anyone learns who judges whom. Like a reef hiding coral in shifting crevices, honest work blends into a crowd an attacker cannot map. Collusion only pays if a fixed jury persists long enough to echo each other's verdicts, but rotation breaks that ledge of trust before it forms. To win, an attacker must bribe a fresh unknown majority every epoch, losing slashed stakes far exceeding any reward, so repeated attacks are guaranteed losses.
